Questions.content: What is the form of \(R(x)\)? Since \(P(x)\) is a monic polynomial of degree 3, what are the degrees and forms of the remainders when divided by quadratic polynomials? This information might affect how the equations in "FormEquations" are set up.

Answers.content:
Since \(P(x)\) is a monic polynomial of degree 3, the remainders when divided by quadratic polynomials will be linear polynomials. Specifically:

- When \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x - 1)(x - 4)\), the remainder \(R(x)\) will be a linear polynomial of the form \(ax + b\).
- Similarly, when \(P(x)\) is divided by \((x - 2)(x - 3)\), the remainder \(2R(x)\) will also be a linear polynomial of the form \(c_1 x + d_1\).

Given that \(2R(x) = c_1 x + d_1\) and knowing \(R(x) = ax + b\), we have:
\[ 2(ax + b) = c_1 x + d_1 \]
This implies:
\[ c_1 = 2a \]
\[ d_1 = 2b \]

Thus, the forms of the remainders are:
- \(R(x) = ax + b\)
- \(2R(x) = 2ax + 2b\)
